Keep September (P), the control: as served in this run, qwen3.8-flash (A) and 1017 (B) each cost more per reply, and neither holds Kairo in character any better.

As served in this run, with no provider recorded, production cost rises by $0.62 per 1,000 replies and $0.49 per 1,000 replies, both clear of zero after correction. Only a candidate cheaper than the control on production routing would reopen the question.

!
Costs are as served in this run: no arm records the provider that served it, and an earlier finding says qwen3.8-flash costs less than the control.
!
Confidence: High, if the caveats below aren't material.
  • No arm records the provider that served it. Only if, on the routing production would use, a candidate cost less than the control's $1.89 per 1,000 replies. Until a re-pricing shows that, keeping the control holds; and even then the call would become a trade, not a switch, because after correction qwen3.8-flash (A) passes 8 points fewer trials and 1017 (B) holds character 5 points less often.
  • The judge is not calibrated. Only if a candidate also proved cheaper on production routing: then whether its character loss is real would decide the call. In this run the cost order, not the judge, decides it; a judge that misread a candidate's style could shrink or erase its character loss, but would not make it cheaper.
  • The aspect was set after the results. Only if a different aspect should have been asked before the run. The cost order that decides the call holds whatever aspect is read.
  • The control was set after the results. Only if another arm should have been the control. September (P) is the least costly of the three arms as served either way.
  • A confound: model. Only if something besides the served model moved between arms. Two things did or may have: 1017 (B)'s reasoning share, carried beside its claims, and the provider, unrecorded for every arm and carried above.
  • The margin was set after the results. The late margin was checked: the call holds at every margin.
  • The floor was set after the results. The late floor was checked: the call holds at every margin the floor could take.
RecommendationKeep September (P) on all traffic. As served in this run it is the least costly arm, at $1.89 per 1,000 replies, and neither candidate shows a gain in character to set against its higher cost.
Why not the othersqwen3.8-flash (A) costs $0.62 per 1,000 replies more as served and passes fewer trials, down 8 points (-13 to -2 after correction). 1017 (B) costs $0.49 per 1,000 replies more as served and holds character less often, down 5 points after correction, though part of that may come from how much it reasoned; on pass rate the evidence cannot tell it and the control apart.
WatchThe weakest margin is qwen3.8-flash (A)'s on the margin on character adherence (v2): at the far end of the 95% interval, adjusted for 16 comparisons, its pass-rate drop reaches 13 points, 2 points inside the line. It bears on a rejected option, not on the call. A prior insight held that qwen3.8-flash lowers production costs; here, as served, it costs more. No arm names its provider, so whether that is the model or this run's routing is unknown: it is the risk the call carries.
NextPrice both candidates on the provider routing production would use. If neither falls below the control's cost, the call stands; if one does, its character loss becomes a trade to price.

As served in this run, both candidates cost more per reply than the control, and the paired intervals exclude zero for each: $0.62 per 1,000 replies more for qwen3.8-flash (A), $0.49 per 1,000 replies more for 1017 (B). 1017 (B) spent a smaller share of its output reasoning (55% against the control's 76%), so its comparison is not at equal reasoning; matching the control's share would more likely widen its cost gap than close it.

Caveats: A confound: reasoning ratio.

The control fails off-lane asks too: of the off-lane trials, three per case over 38 cases, 42 failed for any cause on September (P), against 68 on qwen3.8-flash (A) and 63 on 1017 (B). Off-lane is a weakness of the persona, not only of the candidates.

Off-lane trials failed for any cause, of three per case over 38 cases: 42 on September (P), 68 on qwen3.8-flash (A), 63 on 1017 (B). The cards are every kept one, three per arm, each a nought on holding character, so none shows a trial a check failed. The two match-score cards slip out of the DJ voice in a spoken line; most other cards answer the off-lane ask after brushing it off, one answers it outright, and the laundry cards on every arm, the control's included, give the wash temperature.

On the uncorrected readings, 1017 (B) stops reading as within the margin below 6 points and qwen3.8-flash (A) below 11; on the corrected contrast Watch cites, qwen3.8-flash (A)'s drop reaches 13.

Next steps

  • Price qwen3.8-flash (A) and 1017 (B) on the provider routing production would use, and reconcile with the earlier finding that qwen3.8-flash lowers cost. Whether either candidate can cost less than the control; only then is its character loss a trade worth pricing.
  • Calibrate the judge against human ratings on holding character, weighted toward off-lane asks. Whether the candidates' character losses, and the control's off-lane failures, are real or the judge's reading.
  • Rerun 1017 (B) with its reasoning share matched to the control's. Whether its cost and character gaps belong to the model or to how much it reasoned.
  • Revise the off-lane directive so a brush-off carries no answer, and rerun the off-lane asks on all arms. Whether the stratum that carries the most loss for every arm, the control included, can lift.

Left out, and why

The judge's overall outcome and transcript scores
They point the same way as the pass rate (qwen3.8-flash (A) lower, 1017 (B) cannot be told apart) and do not change the call.
The send-message-or-queue-voice check and failed-reply notices
The evidence cannot tell either candidate and the control apart on them, and neither bears on cost.
Measuring spend across all roles
It counts the evaluation's own spend, judge and simulator included, not what production would pay.
Strata other than off-lane
No other stratum's drop is large enough to lead; most hold ten cases or fewer. They stay in the full tables.
Items delivered, tool provider faults and turns that ran over budget
Telemetry that describes the run, not the persona; none bears on the call.
Cost uplift as a percentage, in the claims
The options table prints it, read off unpaired means; the claims cite the paired dollar gaps instead, and Method reconciles the two.

Method

Cases and repeats
299 cases, each run three times per arm; intervals count cases, not trials, except the off-lane comparisons, which may be too narrow.
What a pass means
A trial passes when its candidate did not fail, every goal check passed and every judged dimension scored at least 3 of 5.
Intervals
Readings against the control are each candidate's own, uncorrected, at 95%. Contrasts are paired by case and corrected together by Holm's method, each at 99.69%, so the whole family's intervals hold together; they read wider than the readings.
Judge
Every judged dimension was scored by openai/gpt-6-luna, with calibration insufficient and zero human ratings.

Caveats: The judge is not calibrated.

Cost basis
Production cost per 1,000 replies, as served in this run; no arm names the provider that served it. The cost gaps the page leads with are paired by case, over the 284 and 293 cases where both arms recorded a cost, so they differ from the gaps between the arms' means ($2.43 per 1,000 replies and $2.41 per 1,000 replies against $1.89 per 1,000 replies); the options table's percentages are read off those unpaired means. Trials with no cost: 33 for the control, 69 for qwen3.8-flash (A), eighteen for 1017 (B). Had each such candidate trial cost nothing, the candidates would still cost $2.24 per 1,000 replies and $2.36 per 1,000 replies, above the control's $2.02 per 1,000 replies had its own cost its p95; the order holds.
Not compared
Latency was read while other runs executed beside it and is left out. Input tokens, output tokens and model calls were not reported.

Caveats: Latency is not compared; Recorded but not reported: input tokens; Recorded but not reported: output tokens; Recorded but not reported: llm calls.

Apparatus
The simulated user's request settings were not recorded on every run, so whether they varied cannot be established.

Caveats: The apparatus may have differed: simulator sent settings.

Declarations
The asked aspect, the control, the margin and the floor were all set on 25 Oct 2026, after the results.

Checks

Send message or queue voice check
The goal check call_count("discord.send_message") >= 1 or call_count("music.queue_voice") >= 1, which code runs on every trial.
